calibration_rulings.title: The title of a beach ("Al-Uqair Beach", "Salwa Beach"), and the noun for a beach against the noun for a coast.
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-beach and salwa-beach: titles and every mention; salwa-beach::practical[1].value through the title's gender (N87). Every later beach page. ROUND 2: uqair-beach::body, the opening clause (round 2's change 3).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A beach is the compound «ساحل سمندر», masculine, written without an izafat sign; a coast is «ساحل». A title whose English translates everything but a place name takes ruling N43's pattern: the place name as its key, the Urdu possessive, the generic — «العقیر کا ساحل سمندر», «سلویٰ کا ساحل سمندر». It inflects like any phrase («العقیر کے ساحل سمندر پر», «العقیر کا تاریخی ساحل سمندر»). After its first mention the beach may be taken up as «یہ ساحل». AMENDED IN ROUND 2: where the source sets the coast and the beach in ONE CLAUSE, the Gulf's shore is said with «کنارہ» — «خلیج کے کنارے کنارے العقیر کا تاریخی ساحل سمندر پھیلا ہوا ہے» (round 2's change 3) — so that «ساحل» is not said twice in the clause: both readers read that clause twice (first reader, item 20; second reader, item 16). «خلیج کے کنارے» is approved text for the Gulf's shore (al-uqair body, two interface strings) and stands twice more on uqair-beach and once on salwa-beach. A coast named for itself stays «ساحل»: «العقیر کا ساحل» (the area line), «العقیر کے ساحل پر» (faq[3].a), the approved «خلیج کا ساحل» of al-uqair and uqair-castle. What is left of the cost on uqair-beach, charged under compliance: «ساحل» is the coast in the area line and the last answer and the beach in «یہ ساحل». The press forms («العقیر بیچ», «العقیر ساحل») are recorded for search and never written. ROUND 2: the titles and the generic are confirmed on two readers. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. The clause round 2 amended, which two readers had read twice, was read once by the third; the rule for a clause that names both the Gulf's shore and the beach stands as amended. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). No published page carries the leaves of uqair-beach that this entry names; what the entry says of them is the record of the round and binds the page when it is applied, after its own proof pass and blind read. On the published pages this entry is carried by salwa-beach: title, summary, body, and practical[1].value through the title's gender. ‖ b11 (2026-10-14): SUPERSEDED — the HELD line above no longer holds. uqair-beach re-entered the chain in batch b11 after the owner decided N100, was read by fresh blind readers of b11 and scored afresh (91), and is applied with b11; its leaves named in this entry are published text.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the title of a beach is the place name's key, the possessive and the two-word generic; the bare «ساحل» is a coast, or takes up a beach already named on the page. In a clause that also names the beach, the Gulf's shore is said with the word of round 2's change 3, not with «ساحل».

calibration_rulings.title: Three loan-free forms under the owner's rule on loans (P16) and its test (P16-test): four-wheel drive, caravan, booking.
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar::practical[1].value (round 1's change 3). uqair-beach::practical[0].label, practical[0].value, faq[0].q, faq[0].a (round 1's changes 6, 7, 9 and 10), until the owner decides item N100-caravan-loan-or-description. uqair-beach::practical[0].value and faq[0].a for the booking verb (unchanged since stage 1). Every later page that names a four-wheel-drive vehicle or a booking.
calibration_rulings.ruling: The test of ruling P16-test applied to each form, condition by condition. This is the ONE account of it and replaces what round 1 said in three places in three ways (proof pass on round 1, finding 2). (1) FOUR-WHEEL DRIVE: THE LOAN STANDS — «فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑی», plural «فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑیاں»; the cell is «صرف فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑی سے». Condition 1 (the native wording is not what the thing is called, shown by the press): met — the Gulf's Urdu paper writes the loan of exactly such vehicles and no native name was found anywhere; the nine-word description was a coinage of this chain. Condition 2 (a blind reader misled): met — the first reader took the native description for any four-wheeled car, on a guarded fact, graded serious. Condition 3 (a dictionary headword OR solid reference attestation): MET IN ITS SECOND, WEAKER CLAUSE ONLY — there is NO dictionary headword; there are five reference pages, two of them running text, and one press page. The test is therefore met as it was for «براؤزر» in b0-ui ('pending: reference attestation only'), and it is NOT the case that all three conditions are met in full: round 1's change 3 and its reader ruling 14 say so in those words and are to be read with this sentence. CONFIRMED BY THE SECOND READER: he read the cell as four-wheel drive only and repeats it in his own words (his items 12 and 36). FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER, because his own rule (P16) is narrower than the test — a loan enters only with an entry that cites a dictionary headword: this is the one loan of the batch admitted on press and reference attestation WITHOUT a headword, and its entry is pending for that reason. If he will have no loan here, the loan-free cell is «صرف چاروں پہیوں کے زور پر چلنے والی گاڑی سے», which a reader took for any car. What decided is the fact: this is the condition he guards with 'only' (build check C37). The figure-and-letter form '4x4' is not written. (2) CARAVAN: the first native description is WITHDRAWN (it reads as a resident's car) and the second, «گھر نما گاڑی» (feminine, plural «گھر نما گاڑیاں»), STANDS IN THE TEXT. What the vehicle is to be called is no longer ruled here: it is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description, with the evidence of both readers and of the press page read in round 2. No third description is coined. (3) BOOKING: THE NATIVE VERB STAYS — «جگہ آن لائن محفوظ کرائی جاتی ہے». Condition 3 is met for the loan (a dictionary headword). Condition 2 is met in its weak form since round 2: the second reader stopped on «محفوظ کرائی» to work out that it means booking, because the same word is the save button and the reserve on these pages; the first reader understood it at once. Condition 1 is NOT shown: the press page read in round 2 writes the loan, but «محفوظ کرانا» is standard written Urdu for reserving a place, and one page that uses the loan does not show that the native verb is not what the act is called. ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, one line: candidate B, «آن لائن بکنگ ہوتی ہے», the word both readers say. ROUND 3: unchanged in all three parts. (1) The loan for the four-wheel-drive vehicle is CONFIRMED BY TWO READERS OF TWO and stays flagged for the owner for want of a headword. (2) The caravan is item N100. (3) The booking verb stays: three readers of three would say the loan, one understood the native verb at once, one stopped on it, one finds it stiff, and nobody misread it; condition 1 of the test is where round 2 left it. It goes to the owner with the caravan, as one question about one row. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). No published page carries the leaves of uqair-beach that this entry names; what the entry says of them is the record of the round and binds the page when it is applied, after its own proof pass and blind read. On the published pages this entry is carried by asfar::practical[1].value, the four-wheel-drive cell, and by nothing else: the caravan and the booking verb stand on uqair-beach alone. ‖ b11 (2026-10-14): SUPERSEDED — the HELD line above no longer holds. uqair-beach is applied with b11 (scored afresh 91); part (2) is settled by the owner's decision in N100 («گھر نما گاڑی»), and part (3), the booking verb «جگہ آن لائن محفوظ کرائی جاتی ہے», stands on uqair-beach as published text — read as 'saved' by the b11 readers, its recorded cost.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker (read from this entry by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs): none of «چاروں پہیوں کے زور پر», «فور بائی فور» occurs; «بکنگ» is not an admitted loan; «کیمپر» is not an admitted loan. The withdrawn description of the caravan is a retired key of this entry. For the proofreader, checklist item 9: the admitted loan is the termbase entry for the four-wheel-drive vehicle, which cites P16; on asfar the word for "only" is the first word of the access cell.

calibration_rulings.title: What is a caravan called on /ur/ — the vehicle one lives in, Arabic «عربات الكرفان», a loan in the source itself: the native description that stands in the text, or a loan?
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-beach::practical[0].label, practical[0].value, faq[0].q, faq[0].a — unchanged from round 1 until the owner decides. Every later page that names a caravan.
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE WORDING, ruled for the text until the owner answers: A stands in the four leaves — «گھر نما گاڑیاں» (label), «گھر نما گاڑیوں کے لیے» (value and answer), «گھر نما گاڑی میں» (question). It is the one wording a reader has decoded without being misled, and no third description is coined (round 1's rule, kept). THE NAME is the OWNER'S DECISION, because his rule on loans (P16) is what stands between the page and the word both readers say: does a caravan take the loan «کارواں» on /ur/? If yes: B in the four leaves, with its noun where the bare word could be read as a party of travellers — label «کارواں گاڑیاں», «کارواں گاڑیوں کے لیے», «کارواں گاڑی میں» — a termbase entry that cites P16 and says, as the four-wheel-drive entry does, that it rests on press and reference attestation without a headword in this sense; and a proof pass and a blind read of the four leaves. If no: A stays as it is, with its cost on record (a reader is stopped by the label and says nobody calls the thing so). THE JUDGE'S RECOMMENDATION, for what it is worth to him: B — the source itself writes the loan, two readers of two name it unprompted, and the paper his readers read writes it. ROUND 3: unchanged — A stands in the four leaves and the name is the owner's decision. The recommendation is firmer by one reader: B. With it goes the booking verb of the same row (item N90), which all three readers would say with the loan. If he admits either, the leaves of uqair-beach that change need their own proof pass and blind read. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN. The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 1): N100, uqair-beach: does a caravan take the loan «کارواں» on /ur/? Three readers of three write it; «گھر نما گاڑی» stops each reader and is decoded from its row. With it, the same row's verb for booking: all three would say the loan (N90). ‖ THE JUDGE'S ADDENDUM to round 3 (section 6), after a fourth reader: stopped and decoded by three readers of three; «کارواں» written by three readers of four, the fourth writes two other loans. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). No published page carries the leaves of uqair-beach that this entry names; what the entry says of them is the record of the round and binds the page when it is applied, after its own proof pass and blind read. No published page carries a wording of this entry. ‖ OWNER DECIDED 2026-10-14: the owner chose «گھر نما گاڑی» — the wording of this entry (label «گھر نما گاڑیاں», value and answer «گھر نما گاڑیوں کے لیے», question «گھر نما گاڑی میں»). uqair-beach leaves HELD; it takes a proof pass and a blind read and is scored afresh before it is applied. ‖ b11 (2026-10-14): SUPERSEDED — the HELD line above no longer holds. uqair-beach is applied with b11, its four leaves in the owner's wording, read by fresh blind readers of b11 (each stopped at the label and would write a loan; recorded, not reopened) and scored afresh (91).

calibration_rulings.title: zaki-alsalem-farm's title: the possessive (N122 (2)) or the compound (N85)?
calibration_rulings.binds: zaki-alsalem-farm::title, body; the key «زکی السالم کا فارم». Every later private place named after its owner.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «زکی السالم کا فارم», masculine. A private farm named after its owner falls under N122 (2)'s reason — the ownership is what the Arabic construct «مزرعة زكي السالم» says, and the RU genitive agrees; N85's compound stays for places named in HONOUR of a person and is not touched. The reader used the title throughout and did not read «زکی» or «السالم» as common words (no remark). B on record. ‖ ROUND 2: Unchanged; no remark from the second reader on the title.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader: the title key byte for byte in title and body; a private place named after its owner carries «کا» after the name (N122 (2)); a place named in honour of a person carries none (N85).

calibration_rulings.title: The frame of a P3b name met in running text with its generic ('countryside chalets known as Aryaf Zaki'): a naming clause or the «نامی» template?
calibration_rulings.binds: zaki-alsalem-farm::body; the key «اریاف زکی». Every later P3b name the source introduces with its generic and a naming verb.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the generic first, the quoted name and its gloss in a naming clause — «… دیہی جھونپڑیاں بنائی گئی ہیں جو “اریاف زکی” (زکی کا دیہی علاقہ) کہلاتی ہیں۔» — the source's own 'known as', N107's frame. P3b's guard is met (marks at the one mention, the gloss once, straight after the closing mark) and P3b (3) is met by the generic standing as the antecedent of the clause that names it. The «نامی» template belongs to P15 (heritage villages) and P3c (2) (a «سوق» / «عین» name met in passing); role file 05 item 10's «نامی» clause is not owed where the generic already governs a naming clause, and B would stack «دیہی علاقہ) نامی دیہی». The reader: the marks and the bracket 'do work: I understood it is a name with a gloss' (item 19). B on record. ‖ ROUND 2: Unchanged; the second reader too read the marks and the bracket as a name and its gloss (item 17). EXCEPTION TO ROLE FILE 05, ITEM 10, for ap-meta to enter in this ruling's note: 'Role file 05, item 10, asks that a P3b name be followed, after its gloss, by «نامی» and its generic. Where the generic already stands as the antecedent of a naming clause («… جو “…” (…) کہلاتی ہیں», N107's frame), that clause discharges P3b (3) and the «نامی» clause is not owed; a proofreader applying item 10 reads it with this exception (b11, N170).'
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader: «“اریاف زکی”» in marks at every mention, its gloss once straight after the closing mark; the generic that says what it is stands either as the antecedent of a naming clause («جو … کہلاتی ہیں») or after «نامی» — one of the two, not both.

calibration_rulings.title: 'Bedouin' (of the women who sell): «بدو», «صحرا نشین» or «بادیہ نشین»?
calibration_rulings.binds: women-souq::body, faq[2].a; the key «بادیہ نشین» (retires «بدو»). Every later mention of the Bedouin on /ur/.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C («بادیہ نشین», stage 4's letter; the fallback round 1 named), ROUND 2. THE TWO READERS: the first (on-05) read «شہری بھی اور بدو بھی» in body and faq[2].a with no remark; the second (on-r1, item 6, moderate) heard «بدو» as 'mildly dismissive ("uncouth")' in a respectful line about women sellers — exactly the trigger stage 4 named ('if a reader hears contempt or "uncouth" in «بدو», the judge replaces it by «بادیہ نشین» in both leaves') and round 1 kept. One reader of two, but the cost is the worst a word can do on this page, and the references carry it (ur.wikipedia's own lead of «بدو», rekhta's «بدوی» 'uncouth'). «بادیہ نشین» is neutral in the reference («عرب کے بادیہ نشین قبائل», 7 pages, HTTP 200, stage 4); the pair stays two nouns of a kind. The reader's «صحرائی (بدوی)» brings «بدوی» back; «بادیہ کی» unbalances the pair. Changes 0, 1; UNREAD — the next reader tests it. The key «بدو» is RETIRED. B «صحرا نشین» stays refused (rekhta: 'hermit'). ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; its list for the owner puts the question this ruling concerns; entered with its question stated, as b8, b9 and b10 entered theirs). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, item 2): women-souq: 'Bedouin' is now «بادیہ نشین» on /ur/ — a reader heard «بدو» as dismissive; say if you prefer another word ‖ ADDENDUM (b11, round 2): the third reader (on-r2, item 8, minor) read «بادیہ نشین» in body and faq[2].a: "bookish and Persianized. I understood it, but it is not how one speaks of people today" — meaning taken, no tone fault; three readers in all: «بدو» passed by the first, 'uncouth' to the second, «بادیہ نشین» understood and called bookish by the third. C stands; its register cost is charged on women-souq.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the retired key «بدو» does not occur. For the proofreader: «بادیہ نشین» in the pair with «شہری»; «صحرا نشین» and «بدوی» do not occur.

calibration_rulings.title: 'At the heart of the old Suwaiq market area': where 'old' stands, and the «نامی» form.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «سوق السویق نامی بازار کے پرانے علاقے کے وسط میں» (body, faq[1].a) — P3c (2)'s required form for a «سوق» name met in passing, 'old' on the area as the English reads the Arabic. COST, charged under nativeness and fit: the reader hears 'market' twice and asks whether he is to find a market inside a market (item 6, moderate); the source itself places the souq at the heart of an older market quarter. calibration_rulings.title: 'Countryside chalets' («أكواخ ريفية»): «دیہی جھونپڑیاں» or «دیہی کٹیائیں»?
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «دیہی جھونپڑیاں», feminine plural — the Arabic authority's own noun. COST, charged on accuracy, nativeness and fit: the reader read 'shabby huts' before the setting told him they are rustic chalets (item 18, moderate) — the cost stage 4 named. Not changed: B «کٹیا» is unverified and as humble; the loan «کاٹیج» is refused (P16); his 'rooms' changes the thing; 'rural-style huts' would add a claim of style that neither source makes. EN 'chalets' against AR 'huts' is logged for the owner. ‖ ROUND 2: Unchanged: the second reader made no remark on «جھونپڑیاں» (one reader of two read shacks); the fallback condition ('a second reader also reads shacks') is not met. Cost stays charged on zaki-alsalem-farm. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; its list for the owner puts the question this ruling concerns; entered with its question stated, as b8, b9 and b10 entered theirs). (N175) ‖ ADDENDUM (b11, round 2): the third reader (on-r2, item 17, moderate) read «دیہی جھونپڑیاں» as poor shacks and offered «دیہاتی طرز کی جھونپڑیاں»; two readers of three. calibration_rulings.title: A summary that is a noun phrase in both sources and whose Urdu puts two locatives before the head noun and a relative clause after it.
calibration_rulings.binds: women-souq::summary. Every later summary of the same build.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, FINAL. A summary that is a noun phrase in both sources stays one (b6 addendum, 1c) EXCEPT where the Urdu's order puts two or more locatives before the head noun and a relative clause after it, so that the reader hunts for the main verb: then the head noun takes «ہے» and the locatives read as an existential sentence. Nothing enters: «ہے» says the place is there, which the noun phrase presupposes; no pronoun is added. THE TWO READERS: the first read the noun phrase twice to find its subject (on-05 item 1, moderate); the second read the edited summary «… پتھاروں کا ایک روایتی بازار ہے، جہاں …» with no remark on its build (on-r1; his item 2 is on the unchanged relative clause). C (the reader's pronoun frame) not taken.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: such a summary closes its head noun with «ہے» and adds no other word; a noun-phrase summary without stacked locatives before its head stays a noun phrase.
